svg.title: The stages of labour
svg.desc: A horizontal timeline of labour in three stages, with the EMT decision point marked. FIRST STAGE runs from the onset of regular contractions to full dilation of the cervix and is the longest stage; contractions become longer, stronger and closer together; the membranes may rupture; this is usually the stage in which there is time to transport. SECOND STAGE runs from full dilation to the delivery of the baby; the mother feels an urge to push or to bear down, and CROWNING appears - the head visible at the opening. THIRD STAGE runs from the delivery of the baby to the delivery of the placenta, which separates and delivers on its own. A decision box between the first and second stages reads CROWNING DECIDES IT: if the head is visible you deliver where you are, because transporting gives the same event with less room, light and hands. A footer notes that the mother is the patient who gets forgotten and is the one who bleeds, and that durations vary enormously and are not stated.
svg.text: Three stages, and one decision that sits between the first two.
Onset of regular contractions → full dilation
Usually the stage with time to transport
Full dilation → delivery of the baby
An URGE TO PUSH or to bear down
Delivery of the baby → delivery of the placenta
The placenta separates and delivers ON ITS OWN
It goes IN A BAG and travels with you
Watch for bleeding · massage the uterus per protocol
Everybody looks at the baby. That is what happens,
THE MOTHER IS THE ONE WHO GETS FORGOTTEN
and she is the one who bleeds. Turn round and
Durations vary enormously between people and between pregnancies, and no figures are given here for that reason.
Confirm the stages, the findings and your own delivery procedure against the current text and your local protocol.
Suction practice at delivery has changed and varies by system — follow your own protocol rather than what you have seen.
